# Threat Model Pack v0.2

**Version:** 2026-05-24
**Status:** POC owner decision pass recorded; Slices A, B, D, E, F, and G reconciled
**Generated by:** `/threat-model` skill (see `~/.claude/skills/threat-model/SKILL.md` for format spec)

This pack documents the current ThreatPrism security model before adding memory, RAG, write-back, dashboard UI, live LLM provider calls, tool/function-calling, multi-tenancy, or production identity integrations.

ThreatPrism is modeled here as an internal SOC AI-assisted case and report analysis system for organizations moving from outsourced SOC operations toward an internal SOC model. The current implementation is demo-safe, fake-data only, and analyst-controlled.

---

## What Changed in v0.2

| Element | v0.1 | v0.2 |
|---------|------|------|
| Framework selection | Implicit | Explicit per-component table in [`system-context.md`](system-context.md) |
| Severity ratings | None | Likelihood × Impact rubric applied to every threat |
| Mitigation pointers | Component-level ("demo auth") | Function-level with line numbers (e.g., `authorize_role_view()` at [auth/demo.py:73](../../src/threatprism/auth/demo.py)) |
| Residual risk | Mentioned in prose | Dedicated **Residual Risk Register** per file with owner sign-off TODOs |
| Open threats | Mentioned in prose | Dedicated **Open Threats** tables per file with severity and target conditions |
| Pre-implementation gates | Mixed in | Dedicated sections in LLM/LINDDUN files for RAG/memory/tools/tenancy/PHI |
| Review log | Absent | Per-file table tracking versions, reviewers, verdicts |
| Threat identifiers | Free-text descriptions | Structured IDs (`S1`, `L1`, `LD1`, `OT-X`, `RR-X`) cross-referenced in traceability matrix |

The total threat count increased substantially because v0.2 enumerates per-category instead of per-prose-section. STRIDE alone went from 6 prose threats to 15 enumerated entries.

## How to Use This Pack

### As a reviewer
1. Start with [`system-context.md`](system-context.md) for scope and assets.
2. Pick the lens file(s) that match the component you're reviewing.
3. Use [`mitigations-traceability.md`](mitigations-traceability.md) to confirm each mitigation has a test.
4. Add yourself to the Review Log of any file you review.

### As an engineer about to ship a feature
1. Check the **Pre-Implementation Requirements** section of the LLM threat model if you're adding RAG, memory, tools, or multi-tenancy.
2. Check the **Pre-Production Hardening** section of the LINDDUN file if you're adding real PHI handling.
3. Walk your change against the lens files — does it introduce a new trust boundary, attacker surface, or data flow? If yes, re-run `/threat-model` and update the affected files.

### As an operator
1. Read [`SECURITY.md`](../../SECURITY.md) first — that's the production-facing summary.
2. Read [`system-context.md`](system-context.md) for the trust model you're operating under.
3. The Open Threats tables in each lens file list what you need to mitigate operationally (rate limits, body size limits, auth hardening) before networked deployment.

## Critical Findings (Summary)

These are the highest-severity items surfaced in the v0.2 refresh. Each links to its full entry in a lens file.

| Severity | Finding | Source |
|----------|---------|--------|
| **Critical** (post-tools) | OT-L4 — No tool/plugin design exists; required before any function-calling work | [llm-agent-threat-model.md](llm-agent-threat-model.md) |
| **Critical** (real PHI) | OT-LD1 — System is not HIPAA-compliant for real PHI handling | [healthcare-data-threat-model.md](healthcare-data-threat-model.md) |
| **High** (post real-LLM) | RR-L1 — Pattern-based prompt firewall remains bypassable by semantic prompt injection; detected quarantine patterns now block provider execution | [llm-agent-threat-model.md](llm-agent-threat-model.md) |
| **High** | OT-8 — No append-only audit log, no centralized export, no retention policy | [stride-threat-model.md](stride-threat-model.md) |

The unique value of v0.2's format: severity is rated under a rubric, not softened by familiarity. All of these findings were *described* in v0.1 but several were not *rated*.

## Current Architecture Scope

This pack covers the implemented local backend at commit `fea5f9f`:

- FastAPI routes under [src/threatprism/api/app.py](../../src/threatprism/api/app.py)
- Case orchestration under [src/threatprism/cases/service.py](../../src/threatprism/cases/service.py)
- Pydantic response and domain schemas under `src/threatprism/cases/`
- Demo authentication and role authorization under `src/threatprism/auth/`
- Prompt, healthcare, tokenization, role-view, evidence, policy, and action guardrails under `src/threatprism/guardrails/` and `src/threatprism/actions/`
- SQLite demo persistence under `src/threatprism/persistence/`
- Deterministic demo provider under `src/threatprism/llm/`
- Fake SOAR and demo scenario inputs under `examples/`
- Dry-run eval harness and fake fixtures under `src/threatprism/evals/` and `tests/evals/`
- Read-only CSI/RGOI retrieval-governed cognition under `src/threatprism/csi/`

---

## Out of Scope

This pack does not approve or implement:

- Real remediation or containment
- Live LLM, SOAR, cloud, or enrichment calls
- Production IdP, OAuth/OIDC, Entra, or break-glass access
- MSSP multi-tenancy
- Real healthcare, workplace, tenant, host, user, domain, IP, or secret data
- HIPAA compliance, HITRUST certification, audit-ready, or control-satisfied claims

Each of these has a dedicated **Pre-Implementation Requirements** section in the appropriate lens file.

---

## When to Refresh This Pack

Trigger a refresh of the affected file(s) when any of the following happens:

- A new trust boundary is added (new external integration, new role, new auth mode, new data store, new ingress)
- A new attacker surface is introduced (new LLM provider, new file upload, new agent autonomy, new public endpoint)
- A control referenced by an existing model is removed or substantially changed
- The architecture diverges from what the model describes
- A security incident or near-miss reveals a missed threat

To refresh: run `/threat-model` and pick "Refresh of an existing model that is stale" plus the affected file. The skill will diff the model against current code and rewrite only the affected sections.

---

## Validation Path

Use the existing safe local validation wrapper after any documentation or implementation change:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\validate-threatprism.ps1
```

The traceability table ([`mitigations-traceability.md`](mitigations-traceability.md)) names the current test files that cover each implemented mitigation and the proposed test files that should be added before future RAG, memory, write-back, tools, or production integration work.
